land.text: the southern highlands that were 'integrated into the Qatabanian kingdom' until 110 BCE

predecessors.note: The infobox names Qataban as predecessor; the Qataban page adds that Himyar 'joined Saba to form the kingdom of Saba and Dhu-Raydan'.

land.text: Yemen as a Sasanian province under the governor Wahrez, 575/578 to the early 7th century

successors.note: The infobox: successor Sasanian Empire, which annexed Yemen as a province in 575 or 578. The Aksum dossier holds Yemen as an Aksumite vassal 525-570 and has the Sasanian Empire take it in 570-578.

capitals.name: Zafar (Ẓafār)
capitals.note: 'Classical sources give Zafar as the capital.' Aksum held it c. 200-230.

capitals.name: Sanaa
capitals.note: 'Himyarite power eventually shifted to Sanaa as the population increased in the fifth century'; the start year is the century's first, the page gives none. The Persians took Sanaa in 570 (Aksumite-Persian wars page).

keyframe_review.note: 73,575 km2, -110..-67: the southern highlands of Yemen around Zafar. The page has Himyar become an independent kingdom after 110 BCE, when it separated from Qataban (infobox predecessor Qataban); the Qataban page has the Himyarite confederation 'seceded from it around 110 BCE and joined Saʾbaʾ to form the kingdom of Saʾbaʾ and Ḏū-Raydān'. The Himyar page gives no infobox area.

correction.text: the -110 core: the southern highlands, without the northern band; no page extends Himyar north of Najran before the 4th century

keyframe_review.note: 334,765 km2, -66..-37, but 1,028 of its 1,339 cells are a band from 14.7 N to 26.4 N (Asir, Najran, the Hejaz) that no page gives to Himyar in the 1st century BC: the Himyar page's first conquest is Saba c. 25 BCE and its southern-highland kingdom is the -110 core; the Sabaeans dossier gives the Saba cells to Saba until 25 BCE. The -110 core is the shape to use.

correction.text: the -110 core in place of the Cliopatria outline, which has no highlands

keyframe_review.note: 214,510 km2, -36..-32: the shape has lost the Himyarite core (509 of the cells at -66 are the highlands) and keeps only the northern band, which looks like a mislabelled neighbour (the Nabataean sphere). Nothing on the pages opened puts Himyar there or removes it from the highlands. The -110 core is used.
195,907 km2, -31..-26: the same northern band without the highlands; replaced by the -110 core. Saba is conquered c. 25 BCE (Himyar page) in the next step.

correction.text: the highlands plus Saba (Marib), conquered c. 25 BCE

keyframe_review.note: 84,904 km2, -25..-20: the highlands with Qataban's core cells but without Saba. The Himyar page has Saba conquered c. 25 BCE for the first time; the Sabaeans page: 'Greatly economically weakened, the Kingdom of Saba was soon annexed by the Himyarite Kingdom' after Aelius Gallus (26/25 BCE; the Ancient history of Yemen page calls Gallus's campaign in 25 BCE the first absolutely reliable date). The Sabaeans dossier keeps a Sabaean remnant to -20; the Himyar page's year is used, Saba added and Qataban's cells (Qataban was independent until 183 on Cliopatria's row) not.

correction.text: the highlands plus Saba, for -19..99; from c. 100 the Saba cells leave (next verdict)

keyframe_review.note: 334,765 km2, -19..105, the same northern band as -66 plus Saba and Qataban. Saba is Himyar's from c. 25 BCE and 'liberat[ed] itself from Himyar by around 100 CE' (Sabaeans page); no page gives Himyar the northern band or Qataban in these centuries. The highlands plus Saba hold -19..99.

correction.text: the highlands core of 154 (313 cells), Saba independent from c. 100

keyframe_review.note: 149,074 km2, 106..153: still holds Saba (268 cells) and Qataban's core, which the pages do not support: Saba 'liberat[ed] itself from Himyar by around 100 CE' and the Himyar page has Saba and Qataban independent until c. 275 and c. 200 respectively. The highlands core is the shape to use; the Sabaeans dossier adds the 100..153 Sabaean keyframe.

73,629 km2, 154..269: the highlands core. Aksum took Zafar early in the 3rd century (Ancient history of Yemen page) and held 'much of western Yemen' c. 200-230 (Kingdom of Aksum page); the shape is drawn whole and the occupation is a ledger event (the Aksum dossier draws it hatched). Qataban's c. 200 annexation (Himyar page) is not drawn: Qataban's own row runs to 183 and the Hadhramaut dossier takes its land.

73,629 km2, 270..282: unchanged. Saba is 'finally permanently conquered by the Himyarites around 275 CE' (Sabaeans page; 'around 280' on the Himyar page), so the step to the Saba-inclusive shape at 283 is a few years late.
136,986 km2, 283..305: the highlands plus Saba (581 cells). The step matches the Sabaeans page's c. 275 and the Himyar page's c. 280 to within eight years.

295,961 km2, 306..346: adds Hadramawt to 52.2 E. The Himyar page has Hadramawt conquered c. 300 CE; 'By 300' Himyar had defeated Saba, Qataban and Hadramawt, 'uniting the region for the first time'; the Hadhramaut page: it 'ceased to exist by the end of the 3rd century CE, having been annexed by the Himyarite Kingdom'. The step is six years after the pages' c. 300. No page gives an area.

295,961 km2, 347..377, unchanged. The page's expansion to Najd, Kinda and Ma'add rests on Himyarite inscriptions (Ma'add, Mudar, Nizar, Ghassan, tribes near Mecca); the Kinda page does not say Himyar controlled Najd, so it is influence, not territory, and is not drawn.

295,961 km2, 378..533, unchanged for 156 years: the unified Yemen of the 4th-6th centuries. The page has the largest extent in the mid-5th century and again under Abraha; Aksum invaded about 500 and installed Ma'dikarib Ya'fur, Dhu Nuwas ruled from 522, and Kaleb conquered the kingdom in 525-530 (525 on the Dhu Nuwas page). The land is drawn whole through the Aksumite period (the Aksum dossier carries the vassal tint 525-570).

correction.text: the 533 outline for 534..575: Yemen under Aksumite viceroys, then under the Persian vassal Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan

keyframe_review.note: 166.6 km2 (one cell at Najran), 534..576: not a kingdom. The land was Himyarite through the Aksumite viceroys (Sumyafa Ashwa, then Abraha from 531 and Masruq, who continued the Aksumite vice-royalty), until Wahrez's Persians took Sanaa in 570 and Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan reigned as a Persian vassal; the page's infobox ends Himyar in 575/578. The 533 outline is used for 534..575 (and the Aksum dossier tints it as an Aksumite tributary 525-570).

correction.text: the outline unchanged, but belonging to the Sasanian Empire (province of Yemen under the governor Wahrez) from 575; not Himyarite

keyframe_review.note: 295,961 km2, 577..591: the Himyarite outline again, but after 575/578 Yemen is a Sasanian province: Wahrez ended Aksumite overlordship and became 'the hereditary governor of Yemen' (Aksum page) after 'By 575-578' (Aksumite-Persian wars page: 're-conquered Yemen by 578'). Cliopatria's Aksum 534 shape duplicates these 1,291 of 1,292 cells. The land is not Himyar's; the Sasanian Empire takes it.

correction.text: the outline unchanged, but Sasanian Yemen; not Himyarite

keyframe_review.note: 295,961 km2, 592..601: as 577; Greater Yemen stayed under Sasanian control 'until the rise of the Islamic prophet Muhammad in the early 7th century' (Himyar page); the Ancient history of Yemen page adds that Southern Arabia became a Sasanian province under a satrap in 597/598 and that Badhan converted to Islam after 628.

region.text: the southern highlands of Yemen around Zafar, the Himyarite tribal confederation

ledger.note: 110 BC: Himyar becomes an independent kingdom. The Himyar page has it become independent after 110 BCE, when it separated from Qataban (infobox predecessor Qataban); the Qataban page has the Himyarite confederation 'seceded from it around 110 BCE and joined Saʾbaʾ to form the kingdom of Saʾbaʾ and Ḏū-Raydān'.

region.text: Saba with Marib, the Sabaean kingdom

ledger.note: About 25 BC: Himyar conquers Saba for the first time. The Himyar page has Saba conquered c. 25 BCE for the first time; the Sabaeans page: after Aelius Gallus's failed siege of Marib (26/25 BCE) 'Greatly economically weakened, the Kingdom of Saba was soon annexed by the Himyarite Kingdom'.

region.text: Saba, independent of Himyar until c. 275

ledger.note: About 100 AD: Saba breaks free. 'Despite liberating itself from Himyar by around 100 CE', Himyarite kings kept the title 'king of Saba'; Cliopatria's Himyar shape drops the Saba cells at 106.

About 200 AD: Himyar annexes Qataban. The Himyar page has Qataban conquered c. 200 CE while also saying Hadhramaut took Qataban within a few decades of the early 2nd-century split; the Qataban page has Hadramawt and Himyar divide its territory (late 1st or late 2nd century CE) and the Hadhramaut dossier takes the land at 184. The Himyar share cannot be located; Qataban's core is named.

region.text: the Tihama, Najran, al-Ma'afir and Zafar

ledger.note: About 200 AD: Aksum seizes Zafar. Gedara was 'the first king to be involved in South Arabian affairs' and held much of western Yemen, including the Tihama, Najran, al-Ma'afir and Zafar (until c. 230); the Ancient history of Yemen page has Aksum capture Himyar's capital, Zifar, in the first quarter of the century.

About 230 AD: Himyar and Saba push Aksum back. A joint Himyarite-Sabean alliance pushed Aksumite forces back (Aksum page; Zafar held until c. 230; the Ancient history of Yemen page has Himyar retake Zifar and push Aksum back into the Tihama). The af-01 dossier ends its occupation c. 275 on another reading; the page also lists a 'Himyarite-Axumite war of 270-272'.

region.text: Saba, the Sabaean kingdom, ended as a state

ledger.note: About 275 AD: Himyar absorbs Saba for good. The Sabaean kingdom was 'finally permanently conquered by the Himyarites around 275 CE' and 'reverted to a normal tribe'; the Himyar page says 'around 280', and Cliopatria's Himyar shape widens at 283.

region.text: the kingdom of Hadramawt, Shabwa to Dhofar

ledger.note: About 300 AD: Himyar conquers Hadramawt and unites Yemen. Hadramawt 'conquered c. 300 CE'; 'By 300' Himyar had defeated Saba, Qataban and Hadramawt, 'uniting the region for the first time' (Himyar page; the Ancient history of Yemen page: 'around 300 CE'; the Hadhramaut page: 'ceased to exist by the end of the 3rd century CE').
The 5th century: the court moves from Zafar to Sanaa. 'Himyarite power eventually shifted to Sanaa as the population increased in the fifth century' (no year; 401 is the century's first year).

522 AD: the Jewish king Dhu Nuwas takes the throne. He 'rose to power in 522' (the page also allows 518, and the Ancient history of Yemen page c. 517/518), usurping the kingship from Ma'dikarib Ya'fur; the kingdom and its colour continue.

region.text: Himyar, Yemen from the Tihama to Hadramawt, under Aksumite viceroys

ledger.note: 525 AD: Kaleb of Aksum conquers Himyar. Procopius has 'in 525, the armies of the Christian Kingdom of Aksum' invading Yemen (the Himyar page: conquest 'in 525-530'; the Ancient history of Yemen page: Kaleb 'invaded and annexed Yemen' and installed the viceroy Sumyafa Ashwa). Himyar becomes an Aksumite dependency; the tint is drawn from the Aksum ledger (vassal 525-570, gain 520).

531 AD: Abraha makes himself king. He displaced Sumyafa' and declared himself an independent king of Himyar (Ancient history of Yemen page, which has him repair the Marib dam in 543 and reign to at least 547); the Kingdom of Aksum page and the Aksum dossier date the seizure 525 and have him pay tribute.

570 AD: Wahrez's Persians end Aksumite rule in Sanaa. Wahrez came 'at the head of a small expeditionary force of 800 Dailamite cavalrymen in 570 CE' and Masruq was 'personally executed by Wahrez at the Battle of Hadhramaut' (no year); the Ancient history of Yemen page: Aksumite control of Yemen ended with the invasion of the Sassanid general Vahriz in 570.

region.text: Himyar under the vassal king Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan

ledger.note: 570 AD: Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan (Ma'adi Yakrib) is made king under the Sasanians. Khosrow I reinstated him as a Persian vassal after Sanaa fell; he was 'a vassal of the Sasanian Persian Empire' until his Aksumite servants killed him (575 or 578, the page's 'By 575-578').

575 AD: the vassal kingdom ends. Sayf was murdered and Wahrez, with a second army, 'ending Axum rule in Yemen and becoming the hereditary governor of Yemen' (Aksum page: 575; the Himyar page: 575 or 578; the Aksumite-Persian wars page: 're-conquered Yemen by 578').

region.text: Yemen from the Tihama to Hadramawt, the Persian province under the governor Wahrez

ledger.note: 575 AD: Yemen becomes a Sasanian province. The Persians annexed Yemen 'as a province' (Aksumite-Persian wars page; 575 or 578 on the Himyar page); Greater Yemen stayed under Sasanian control 'until the rise of the Islamic prophet Muhammad in the early 7th century'.

region.text: Himyar's land at its end, passing to the Sasanian Empire

ledger.note: 575 AD: the last Himyarite kingdom ends under Sasanian governors. The infobox gives 'Disestablished' as 575/578; the Cliopatria row runs to 601 but its 577-601 shape is the Sasanian province.

wars.name: Aksumite invasion and occupation of western Yemen
wars.outcome: Aksum took Zafar in the first quarter of the 3rd century and held western Yemen until about 230; a Himyarite-Sabaean alliance pushed it back into the Tihama.
wars.note: The Kingdom of Aksum page adds a 'Himyarite-Axumite war of 270-272' without territory.

wars.name: Himyarite-Sabaean wars
wars.outcome: Himyar annexed Saba c. 25 BCE; Saba liberated itself by about 100 CE and 'flourished for another century and a half'; Himyar 'finally permanently conquered' it around 275.

wars.name: Himyarite conquest of Hadramawt
wars.outcome: Himyar invaded Hadramawt in the late 1st century BC and was repelled; Saba took Shabwa in about 225; Himyar conquered Hadramawt about 300.
wars.note: The dates -30 to 225 are the page's 'late 1st century BCE' and 'in 225'.

wars.name: Aksumite intervention of about 500
wars.outcome: Aksum invaded, overthrew the Himyarite king and installed the Christian Ma'dikarib Ya'fur; native Christian kings ruled 500-521/522. No territory is recorded as changing hands.
wars.note: The Dhu Nuwas page does not mention an invasion about 500.

wars.name: Kaleb's invasion of Himyar

zones.text: Zafar, the Tihama coast (Mocha) and Najran, the fighting named on the Dhu Nuwas page

wars.outcome: Kaleb invaded Yemen in 525, Dhu Nuwas was defeated (he died in 530 on the page's infobox, riding 'into the Red Sea' in Ibn Ishaq), Sumyafa Ashwa ruled as viceroy and was displaced by Abraha in 531.
wars.note: The Himyar page says conquest 'in 525-530'; the Aksum page says 518-525 in the infobox and 520 in the text.

wars.name: Aksumite-Persian wars
wars.outcome: Wahrez took Sanaa in 570, defeated Masruq at Hadramawt, and after Sayf's murder annexed Yemen as a Sasanian province by 575-578.

certainty.note: South Arabian frontiers are approximate throughout: the kingdoms are known from inscriptions and the pages give no boundary lines; the Najd and Ma'add tribal claims are influence, not territory.

notes: One state, not split. The Himyar page treats 110 BCE-575/578 CE as one kingdom (named Raydan; kings dhu-Raydan; infobox rows 275-300, 390-420, 510s-530, 535-570, 571-575/578); the early small highland polity and the unified Yemen after c. 300 are phases of it, marked in the ledger by the Saba conquests (25 BCE, 275), Hadramawt (300) and the dynastic renames (522 Dhu Nuwas, 531 Abraha); the seed lists two Seshat ids (ye_himyar_1, ye_himyar_2), whose pages were not opened. The 711-year Cliopatria row is reviewed shape by shape instead. Cliopatria rows that are wrong: -66..-37 and -19..105 carry a northern band to 26.4 N (Asir to the Hejaz) that no page gives to Himyar; -36..-26 has the band without the highlands; 106..153 keeps Saba after it left c. 100; 534..576 is one cell; 577..601 is the Sasanian province and duplicates Cliopatria's Aksum 534 shape (1,291 of 1,292 cells). Disagreements: Qataban's end (Himyar page c. 200; Qataban page late 1st or late 2nd century, divided by Hadramawt and Himyar; Hadhramaut dossier 184); Saba's final conquest (275 Sabaeans page; 280 Himyar page); Abraha's seizure (531 Ancient history of Yemen page; 525 Aksum page and the af-01 dossier); Kaleb's conquest (518/520 Aksum page, 525 Dhu Nuwas and Ancient history pages, 525-530 Himyar page); Dhu Nuwas's death (530 on his infobox); the Persian conquest (570 Wahrez's first expedition; annexation 575 on the Aksum page, 'by 578' on the Aksumite-Persian wars page); Aksum in Yemen c. 200-230 (Aksum page, 'until c. 230') against c. 200-275 in the af-01 dossier. Not drawn: Himyar's tribal sphere in Najd, Kinda and Ma'add (Kinda page: medieval Arabic sources have Himyar's king install Hujr over Ma'add in the late 5th century, but the page does not say Himyar controlled Najd; Kingdom of Kinda has no Cliopatria row and no dossier; the vassal reading would need a page that dates it). The c. 500 Aksumite intervention has no territorial event. Pages that would not load: Aksumite-Himyarite_wars, Hadhramaut_Kingdom (both URL_NOT_FOUND). The Seshat pages were not opened. Counterparts: sabaeans, qataban and hadhramaut have dossiers (me-04); kingdom-of-axum (af-01); sasanian-empire (me-06). No rulers key: the page gives reign dates for only four kings.
